answer: Liveness Beacon Pricing. Each new identity must solve a rotating delay puzzle seeded by a fresh beacon value published per epoch; solutions cannot be precomputed or transferred, so every clone requires its own live compute at the moment of registration. An attacker must forge a separate solution per identity, each binding real hardware time to the beacon. Cost scales linearly with clone count while an honest agent pays once, making cloning dearer than acting alone. Juniper logs hold the seeds for audit.
